reviewed_contracts.contract: SDK API and cold target sample
reviewed_contracts.detail: The pinned headers expose TSession::ExecuteQuery, Basic stats, optional GetStats/GetCompilation and unsigned cache/duration/CPU accessors. Execute and YqlV1 are defaults. Each target uses a fresh one-node TKikimrRunner, after schema/fixture setup. Success requires a present compilation message, from_cache false, positive counters, one result set and zero exit. This is target plan-cache coldness, not cold OS or untouched schema caches.

Pinned main/fixed revision and independent-parent check are delegated to the existing verifier. Receipt profile and target are constrained to the RBO closure, validated before and after. Module and recursive generator/harness/config fingerprints, each input payload digest, generated object/executable identity, receipt bytes and compiler/link environment override hashes are bound. This does not fill the native inherited-environment gap.

reviewed_contracts.contract: Anonymous data transport and bounded serial execution
reviewed_contracts.detail: Adapter source, object, executable, configuration/schema/fixture/target inputs and report use memfds. Rendered SQL is not embedded in generated C++. Native stdout/stderr are redirected before runner creation; report is fixed-field bounded metadata. Input/executable digests are rechecked. The command is behind the existing serial lease. Compile/link/native each run serially in the existing guarded scope with thresholds 24/36/12 GiB, 36 GiB host reserve and scope MemoryMax threshold plus 4 GiB. Actual namespace/socket/temp/spill behavior remains native-pending.

reviewed_contracts.contract: No weakening of direct26 or optimization acceptance
reviewed_contracts.detail: Only anonymous_cpp_verify.main command dispatch changes. All other helper function ASTs match, Q28 still maps to quality_scheduler_cpp_checks and its 26 cases, and pilot schema cannot be a direct-rule record. Semantic/quality/stage-timing/scaling/full-admission flags remain false.

Fields are server-reported compilation wall and scoped CPU counters from the dedicated SDK protobuf, independent of new RBO plan JSON. They exclude startup, fixture execution and final target execution counters. The wall interval includes waits inside compilation but can exclude earlier parse/cache lookup and queue work; CPU is not exhaustive process or pure-RBO CPU. No per-stage or improved-performance claim is justified.
